questions.question: What was the theme of World Tuberculosis Day, 2025, observed in India on 24 March?

options.text: Yes! We Can End TB: Commit, Invest, Deliver
Unite to End TB: Fund, Innovate, Act
End TB Now: Diagnose, Treat, Prevent

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Yes! We Can End TB: Commit, Invest, Deliver**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **World Tuberculosis (TB) Day** is observed annually on **March 24** to raise public awareness about the devastating health, social, and economic consequences of TB and to step up efforts to end the global TB epidemic.
 
• The theme for **World TB Day 2025** is **"Yes! We Can End TB: Commit, Invest, Deliver"**. This theme builds on previous years' messages of hope but adds a specific call to action regarding political **commitment**, financial **investment**, and the **delivery** of care.
 
• The theme emphasizes that ending TB is possible through high-level leadership, increased funding, and faster uptake of new **World Health Organization (WHO)** recommendations to ensure that every patient receives the best standard of care.
 
• The date of **March 24** commemorates the day in **1882** when **Dr. Robert Koch** announced that he had discovered **Mycobacterium tuberculosis**, the bacterium that causes tuberculosis. This discovery was the first step toward diagnosing and curing the disease.
 
• In **India**, the observation of this day is significant as the country has set an ambitious target to eliminate TB by **2025**, five years ahead of the global **Sustainable Development Goal (SDG)** target of **2030**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National TB Elimination Program (NTEP):** Formerly known as the Revised National Tuberculosis Control Program (RNTCP), the **NTEP** is the specialized agency under the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare** responsible for TB control in **India**.
 
• **Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana:** This scheme provides a monthly financial incentive of **Rs. 500** to all TB patients for nutritional support. The payment is made through **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** to the patient's bank account throughout the duration of their treatment.
 
• **Pradhan Mantri TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan:** Launched by the President of India, this initiative aims to bring together all community stakeholders to support those on TB treatment. It introduces the concept of **Ni-kshay Mitras**, who are donors (individuals, NGOs, or corporates) that adopt TB patients to provide nutritional and vocational support.
 
• **Disease Characteristics:** TB is an infectious disease that primarily affects the **lungs** (pulmonary TB), but can also affect other organs such as the **brain**, **kidneys**, and **spine** (extra-pulmonary TB). It spreads through the air when people with lung TB cough, sneeze, or spit.
 
• **Drug-Resistant TB:** One of the biggest challenges in TB elimination is **MDR-TB (Multi-Drug Resistant Tuberculosis)**, where the bacteria do not respond to at least **Isoniazid** and **Rifampicin**, the two most powerful first-line anti-TB drugs. This requires longer and more complex treatment regimens.
 
• **BCG Vaccine:** The **Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG)** vaccine is widely used in **India** as part of the **Universal Immunization Programme** to protect infants and children from severe forms of tuberculosis.
</ul

questions.question: Which new legislation replaced outdated regulatory bodies for healthcare professions (MCI) in India, as reported in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Medical Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Medical Commission (NMC)** was established as the primary regulatory body for medical education and professionals in India, replacing the decades-old **Medical Council of India (MCI)**.
 
• This transition was formalized under the **National Medical Commission Act, 2019**, which received presidential assent on **August 8, 2019**, and officially came into force on **September 25, 2020**.
 
• The primary objective of the **NMC** is to improve access to quality and affordable medical education, ensure the availability of adequate and high-quality medical professionals, and promote equitable and universal healthcare.
 
• It oversees the regulation of medical institutions and practitioners, as well as the conduct of the **National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET)** for admission to undergraduate and postgraduate medical courses.
 
• The commission is also tasked with implementing the **National Exit Test (NEXT)**, which will serve as a common final-year undergraduate medical examination, a licentiate exam to practice medicine, and a basis for admission to postgraduate courses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of the NMC:**
 
 
• The commission consists of **33 members**, including a **Chairperson** (who must be a medical professional), **10 ex-officio members**, and **22 part-time members**.
 
• The members include representatives from the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare**, the **Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS)**, and various **State Medical Councils**.
 
 
 
• **Autonomous Boards:**
 
 
• The **NMC** functions through four distinct autonomous boards: the **Under-Graduate Medical Education Board (UGMEB)**, the **Post-Graduate Medical Education Board (PGMEB)**, the **Medical Assessment and Rating Board (MARB)**, and the **Ethics and Medical Registration Board (EMRB)**.
 
• The **MARB** has the authority to grant permission for establishing new medical colleges and increasing seat capacity, significantly streamlining the **MCI's** previous cumbersome inspection processes.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Scope:**
 
 
• The **NMC** has the power to frame guidelines for determination of fees and all other charges in respect of **50% of seats** in private medical institutions and deemed universities.
 
• It maintains a **National Register** containing the name, address, and all recognized qualifications of licensed medical practitioners in **India**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The **Medical Council of India (MCI)** was originally established in **1933** under the **Indian Medical Council Act, 1933**. It was later reconstituted under the **Indian Medical Council Act, 1956**.
 
• The transition to **NMC** was recommended by a high-level committee chaired by **Arvind Panagariya** and the **Ranjit Roy Chaudhury Committee**, following reports of corruption and lack of accountability within the **MCI**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Community Health Providers:** The **NMC Act** includes a provision for granting limited licenses to **Community Health Providers** to practice medicine at mid-level in the primary healthcare sector, aimed at addressing the shortage of doctors in rural areas.
 
• **Accountability:** Unlike the **MCI**, which was an elected body of doctors, the **NMC** is a government-nominated body, which was intended to increase government oversight and reduce the conflict of interest inherent in a self-regulatory body.
 
• **Uniform Standards:** The commission works to ensure uniform standards of medical education in **India**, aligning them with global benchmarks to facilitate better mobility for **Indian** medical graduates.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following summits in 2025 will be co-hosted by World Health Organization (WHO) and the Ministry of Ayush, Government of India in New Delhi, aiming to strengthen traditional medicine globally?

options.text: Second WHO Global Summit on Traditional Medicine 2025
Global Health and Traditional Medicine Summit 2025

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Second WHO Global Summit on Traditional Medicine 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Second WHO Global Summit on Traditional Medicine** is scheduled to be held in **2025** in **New Delhi**, India, marking a significant milestone in global healthcare collaboration.
 
• This high-level event is co-hosted by the **World Health Organization (WHO)** and the **Ministry of Ayush**, Government of India, reflecting a strong partnership to promote traditional healing systems.
 
• The summit aims to strengthen the **evidence-based integration** of traditional, complementary, and integrative medicine (TCIM) into national health systems and **global health policies**.
 
• It serves as a follow-up to the **First WHO Global Summit on Traditional Medicine**, which took place in **Gandhinagar, Gujarat**, in **August 2023**.
 
• The **2025 summit** will focus on **innovation**, **digital health**, and the application of **modern science** to validate traditional knowledge for the benefit of human health and the planet.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ministry of Ayush:** 
 
 
• The **Ministry of Ayush** was established on **9th November 2014** by the Government of India to ensure the development and propagation of **Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, and Homoeopathy**.
 
• It plays a pivotal role in positioning India as a global leader in **traditional medicine** through research, education, and international partnerships.
 
 
 
• **WHO Global Centre for Traditional Medicine (GCTM):** 
 
 
• Located in **Jamnagar, Gujarat**, the **GCTM** is the first and only global center of its kind established by the **World Health Organization**.
 
• It acts as a **knowledge hub** to catalyze ancient wisdom and modern science for the health of people and the planet, focusing on **evidence, data, and sustainability**.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat Declaration:** 
 
 
• Following the first summit in **2023**, the **Gujarat Declaration** was released, highlighting the global commitment to scaling up the **scientific validation** of traditional medicine.
 
• It emphasizes the role of traditional medicine in achieving **Universal Health Coverage (UHC)** and **Sustainable Development Goal 3 (SDG 3)**.
 
 
 
• **Global Prevalence:** 
 
 
• According to WHO data, approximately **80%** of the world’s population uses **traditional medicine**, and it is a major part of the health economy in many countries.
 
• Nearly **40%** of approved **pharmaceutical products** today are derived from **natural substances**, underlining the importance of biodiversity and traditional knowledge.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **International Classification:** The WHO has integrated traditional medicine modules into the **ICD-11 (International Classification of Diseases)** to enable standardized clinical documentation and **global data collection**.
 
• **Strategic Goals:** The **2025 summit** in **New Delhi** is expected to address the **regulatory frameworks** required for the quality, safety, and efficacy of traditional medicinal products.
 
• **Biodiversity and Sustainability:** A key theme involves the **sustainable sourcing** of medicinal plants and protecting the **intellectual property rights** of indigenous communities who hold traditional health knowledge.
 
• **Technology Integration:** The summit will likely explore how **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** and **Genomics** can be used to study the multi-component nature of traditional formulations.

questions.question: Which of the following DRDO-executed schemes under the ‘Make in India’ initiative provides grants-in-aid to Indian industries (MSMEs/start-ups) for developing defence and dual-use technologies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Technology Development Fund (TDF)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Technology Development Fund (TDF)** is a flagship program of the **Ministry of Defence**, executed specifically by the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** under the **‘Make in India’** initiative.
 
• The primary objective of the **TDF scheme** is to provide **grants-in-aid** to **Indian industries**, including **MSMEs** and **start-ups**, to encourage the design and development of indigenous **defence and dual-use technologies**.
 
• The scheme aims to bridge the gap between R&D and commercialization by supporting the development of **prototypes** or upgrading existing systems to meet the requirements of the **Indian Armed Forces**.
 
• Under this program, the **DRDO** provides financial support up to **90%** of the total project cost. In **June 2022**, the funding limit was significantly enhanced from **₹10 crore** to **₹50 crore** per project to accommodate high-value technology development.
 
• The program is designed to foster a culture of **innovation** and **self-reliance (Aatmanirbharta)** in the defence sector by involving private sector players in cutting-edge technology domains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Innovations for Defence Excellence (iDEX):**
 
 
• Launched in **April 2018**, **iDEX** is aimed at creating an ecosystem to foster innovation and technology development in **Defence and Aerospace**.
 
• It is funded and managed by the **Defence Innovation Organisation (DIO)**, not directly by DRDO.
 
• It provides a platform for **start-ups**, **individual innovators**, and **MSMEs** to solve challenges posed by the Services through the **Defence India Start-up Challenge (DISC)**.
 
 
 
• **Defence Testing Infrastructure Scheme (DTIS):**
 
 
• Launched in **May 2020** with an outlay of **₹400 crore**, this scheme focuses on creating state-of-the-art **testing facilities** in partnership with the private sector.
 
• It aims to promote indigenous production by providing **Greenfield Testing Infrastructure**, particularly in the **Defence Industrial Corridors** of **Uttar Pradesh** and **Tamil Nadu**.
 
 
 
• **Aatmanirbhar Defence Innovation & Technology Initiative (ADITI):**
 
 
• Launched in **March 2024**, **ADITI** is a specialized scheme under the **iDEX** framework to promote **deep-tech** innovations in the defence sector.
 
• It offers grants-in-aid up to **₹25 crore** to eligible start-ups for research and development in critical and strategic technology areas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Eligibility for TDF:** Only **Indian companies** incorporated under the **Companies Act 2013** or **LLP Act 2008** are eligible. The majority stake (at least **51%**) must be held by **Indian citizens**.
 
• **Dual-use Technology:** These are technologies like **advanced sensors**, **AI-based surveillance**, and **drones** that have applications in both **military warfare** and **civilian sectors** (e.g., disaster management or logistics).
 
• **Project Duration:** The maximum development period for a project under the **TDF** is generally **2 years**, ensuring a fast-track approach to technology indigenization.
 
• **Nodal Agency:** While the **Ministry of Defence** provides the mandate, the **Directorate of TDF** within **DRDO** acts as the nodal agency for evaluation and implementation.

questions.question: Nag Mk 2 Missile has been developed by which organisation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Defence Research and Development Organisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Nag Mk 2** is a **third-generation** **Anti-Tank Guided Missile (ATGM)** that has been indigenously designed and developed to strike enemy tanks with high precision.
 
• It is developed by the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)**, specifically through its premier lab, the **Defence Research and Development Laboratory (DRDL)**, located in **Hyderabad**.
 
• The missile is equipped with **Fire-and-Forget** capability, which means that once the missile is locked onto a target and launched, it guides itself automatically without further intervention from the operator.
 
• It uses an advanced **Imaging Infra-Red (IIR)** seeker to track and hit targets during both day and night, ensuring operational efficiency in diverse weather conditions.
 
• The development of the **Nag Mk 2** version focuses on enhanced performance, including improved seeker technology and a more efficient propulsion system compared to its predecessors. ***Hence, the correct answer is Defence Research and Development Organisation.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation):**
 
 
• Established in **1958**, it is the R&D wing of the **Ministry of Defence**, Government of India.
 
• It aims to empower India with cutting-edge defense technologies and achieve self-reliance in critical military systems and platforms.
 
• It was formed by merging the **Technical Development Establishment (TDEs)** and the **Directorate of Technical Development & Production (DTDP)** with the **Defence Science Organisation (DSO)**.
 
 
 
• **Variants of Nag Missile:**
 
 
• **NAMICA (Nag Missile Carrier):** This is a modified **BMP-2** infantry combat vehicle designated as a "tank destroyer," equipped with a thermal sight and a launcher for **Nag** missiles.
 
• **Helina:** It is the helicopter-launched version of the Nag missile, boasting a range of **7 to 10 kilometers**. It is designed to be launched from the **HAL Rudra** and **Light Combat Helicopter (LCH)**.
 
• **Dhruvastra:** This is the Air Force version of the **Helina** missile, recently tested for integration with **Advanced Light Helicopters (ALH)**.
 
 
 
• **Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (IGMDP):**
 
 
• The **Nag** missile was one of the five missile systems envisioned under the **IGMDP**, spearheaded by **Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam** in **1983**.
 
• The other four missiles under this program are **Prithvi** (Surface-to-surface), **Agni** (Ballistic missile), **Trishul** (Short-range surface-to-air), and **Akash** (Medium-range surface-to-air).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Operational Capabilities:** The **Nag** missile features a **top-attack capability**, allowing it to strike the turret of a tank, which is typically the most vulnerable part with the thinnest armor.
 
• **Range:** The land-based version has a minimum range of **500 meters** and an effective maximum range of up to **4 kilometers**.
 
• **Strategic Significance:** The successful induction of such indigenous systems strengthens India’s **Atmanirbhar Bharat** initiative in the **Defence Sector** and reduces dependency on foreign imports for anti-tank weaponry.
</ul

questions.question: Which theme was celebrated for World Malaria Day on 25 April 2025?

options.text: Time to Beat Malaria: Reinvest, Reimagine, Reignite
Malaria Ends with Us: Reinvest, Reimagine, Reignite
Invest in Malaria-Free Future: Reinvest, Reimagine, Reignite
Zero Malaria Starts with Me: Reinvest, Reimagine, Reignite

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Malaria Ends with Us: Reinvest, Reimagine, Reignite**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **World Malaria Day** is an international observance commemorated every year on **25 April** to recognize global efforts to control and eventually eliminate malaria.
 
• For the year **2025**, the theme is **"Malaria Ends with Us: Reinvest, Reimagine, Reignite"**. This theme serves as a clarion call for the global community to bolster its commitment toward a malaria-free world.
 
• The **"Reinvest"** aspect of the theme emphasizes the critical need for increased domestic and international funding to close the gap in malaria financing, which has stagnated in recent years.
 
• The **"Reimagine"** component encourages the development and deployment of innovative tools, such as **next-generation insecticide-treated nets**, **gene-drive mosquitoes**, and more effective **vaccines**.
 
• The **"Reignite"** pillar focuses on restoring political will and community engagement to get the world back on track toward the **2030** targets of the **Global Technical Strategy for Malaria**.
 
• This observance provides an opportunity for affected countries to share their experiences and for international partners to showcase progress in research and development.

questions.question: Which Ministry of the Government of India carried out the Management Effectiveness Evaluation (MEE) for 2020-2025?

options.text: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** is the nodal agency in the administrative structure of the Central Government for the planning, promotion, coordination, and overseeing the implementation of India's environmental and forestry policies and programmes.
 
• The **Management Effectiveness Evaluation (MEE)** for the cycle **2020-2025** represents the **5th cycle** of assessment for **National Parks** and **Wildlife Sanctuaries** in India.
 
• This evaluation process is conducted by the **MoEFCC** with technical support from the **Wildlife Institute of India (WII)**, an autonomous institution based in **Dehradun**.
 
• The primary objective of **MEE** is to assess how well **Protected Areas** are being managed and whether they are achieving the goals for which they were established.
 
• For the **2020-2025** cycle, the evaluation framework involves a set of **30 indicators** categorized under six elements: **Context, Planning, Inputs, Process, Outputs, and Outcomes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Management Effectiveness Evaluation (MEE):**
 
 
• It is a global tool adopted from the **IUCN World Commission on Protected Areas (WCPA)** framework to evaluate the management efficiency of conservation sites.
 
• India is one of the few countries in the world that has institutionalized the **MEE** process for its network of **Protected Areas** since **2006**.
 
• The evaluation helps in identifying gaps in management and provides a roadmap for future conservation strategies at both the state and national levels.
 
 
 
• **Wildlife Institute of India (WII):**
 
 
• Established in **1982**, **WII** provides scientific knowledge and personnel for the conservation of wildlife in the country.
 
• It plays a critical role in developing the **MEE** scorecard and training the independent expert committees that visit the field sites for data collection.
 
 
 
• **Tiger Reserves and MEE-TR:**
 
 
• Apart from general Protected Areas, the **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)** also carries out a separate **Management Effectiveness Evaluation of Tiger Reserves (MEE-TR)** every four years.
 
• The **MEE** of **Tiger Reserves** follows a similar methodology but focuses specifically on the **54 Tiger Reserves** currently present in India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Rating Scale:** The sites evaluated under **MEE** are given scores and categorized into four ratings: **Very Good** (75% and above), **Good** (60-74%), **Satisfactory** (50-59%), and **Poor** (less than 50%).
 
• **MEE of Zoos (MEE-ZOO):** Recently, the **MoEFCC** also extended this evaluation framework to **Zoos** in India, aiming to improve the standards of animal housing, healthcare, and conservation breeding.
 
• **Data Facts:** India has a network of over **900 Protected Areas**, including **106 National Parks** and **573 Wildlife Sanctuaries**. The **5th cycle** aims to provide a comprehensive look at the health of these ecosystems following the **Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022**.
 
• **Global Commitments:** These evaluations assist India in meeting its international obligations under the **Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)** and the **Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework**.
</ul

questions.question: As announced in the April 2025 Monetary Policy Committee meeting, the Reserve Bank of India aims to keep liquidity surplus close to what percentage of deposits?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** meeting held in **April 2025**, the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** emphasized its commitment to fine-tuning liquidity management to ensure economic stability.
 
• The **RBI** aims to keep the **liquidity surplus** (or deficit) in the banking system close to **1%** of the **Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL)**, which represent the total **deposits** held by banks.
 
• This **1%** target is crucial because it helps the **Weighted Average Call Rate (WACR)** stay aligned with the **Policy Repo Rate**, preventing extreme volatility in the short-term money market.
 
• To achieve this, the **central bank** employs various tools under the **Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF)**, primarily through **Variable Rate Repo (VRR)** and **Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR)** auctions.
 
• The strategy reflects the **RBI's** shift towards a more nimble liquidity management approach, moving away from the massive surpluses seen during the **COVID-19 pandemic** era to a more balanced "neutral" stance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL):**
 
 
• **NDTL** is the sum of **demand liabilities** (like current deposits and demand drafts) and **time liabilities** (like fixed deposits and recurring deposits) minus the deposits held with other banks.
 
• It serves as the fundamental metric for determining the **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)** and **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)** requirements for commercial banks in **India**.
 
 
 
• **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC):**
 
 
• The **MPC** is a **six-member** body constituted by the **Central Government** under **Section 45ZB** of the **RBI Act, 1934**.
 
• It is chaired by the **Governor of the Reserve Bank of India** and meets at least **four times a year** to decide on benchmark interest rates to maintain **inflation** within the target range of **4% (+/- 2%)**.
 
 
 
• **Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) Corridor:**
 
 
• The **LAF corridor** is defined by the **Marginal Standing Facility (MSF)** rate at the upper end and the **Standing Deposit Facility (SDF)** rate at the lower end.
 
• In **2022**, the **SDF** replaced the fixed-rate reverse repo as the floor of the corridor to absorb liquidity without the need for collateral.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Weighted Average Call Rate (WACR):** This is the **operating target** of the **RBI's** monetary policy. It represents the rate at which banks lend to each other in the **overnight call money market**.
 
• **Frictional vs. Structural Liquidity:** The **RBI** distinguishes between **frictional liquidity** (temporary fluctuations due to tax payments or government spending) and **structural liquidity** (long-term trends influenced by foreign exchange flows or currency in circulation).
 
• **Price Stability and Growth:** The primary mandate of the **RBI** is to maintain **price stability** while simultaneously supporting the objective of **economic growth**. Managing the liquidity surplus at **1%** ensures there is enough credit available for the productive sectors of the economy without fueling **inflationary** pressures.
 
• **Financial Year 2025-26:** The **April 2025** meeting sets the tone for the **financial year**, influencing how commercial banks set their **MCLR (Marginal Cost of Funds Based Lending Rate)** and external benchmark-linked lending rates.
</ul

questions.question: In 2025, which of the following Bills was passed by Karnataka to strengthen child protection by outlawing not only child marriage but also betrothal of minors?

options.text: Prohibition of Child Marriage (Karnataka Amendment) Bill, 2025

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prohibition of Child Marriage (Karnataka Amendment) Bill, 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Karnataka Legislative Assembly** passed the **Prohibition of Child Marriage (Karnataka Amendment) Bill, 2025**, to provide a more stringent legal framework to eradicate the practice of child marriage within the state.
 
• A landmark provision of this **2025 Amendment** is that it explicitly outlaws the **betrothal** (engagement) of **minors**. By criminalizing the formal promise of marriage involving a child, the state aims to intervene at an earlier stage before the actual marriage ceremony takes place.
 
• The bill mandates that every child marriage performed in the state shall be **void ab initio** (legally null and void from the beginning). This removes the previous legal ambiguity where some marriages were considered "voidable" rather than automatically void.
 
• It significantly enhances the **punishment** for those who perform, abet, or promote child marriages or betrothals. The offense is categorized as **cognizable and non-bailable**, allowing the police to make arrests without a warrant and making it harder for offenders to secure immediate bail.
 
• The bill empowers **Child Marriage Prohibition Officers** and local authorities with more administrative teeth to act upon reports of planned child marriages or betrothals effectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 (Central Act):**
 
 
• This is the **parent legislation** enacted by the **Parliament of India** to replace the Child Marriage Restraint Act of 1929.
 
• Under the **2006 Act**, the minimum age for marriage is **18 years for females** and **21 years for males**.
 
• While the central act focuses on the ceremony, the **Karnataka Amendment of 2025** expands this scope to include **pre-marriage rituals** like betrothal to ensure comprehensive protection.
 
 
 
• **Socio-Legal Implications:**
 
 
• The inclusion of **betrothal** in the law targets deep-rooted social customs where children are "promised" to families at a **young age**, which often leads to school dropouts and early pregnancies.
 
• According to **NFHS-5 (National Family Health Survey)** data, while child marriage rates have declined, certain districts in **North Karnataka** still show higher-than-average incidences, necessitating state-specific amendments.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional and International Context:**
 
 
• The bill aligns with **Article 21** (Right to Life and Personal Liberty) and **Article 39(f)** of the **Constitution of India**, which directs the state to ensure children are protected against exploitation.
 
• It also serves **Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 5.3**, which aims to eliminate all harmful practices, such as child, early, and forced marriage, by the year **2030**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Betrothal Defined:** In the context of this bill, **betrothal** refers to any ceremony or contract where a child is pledged in marriage. This is now a **punishable offense** in Karnataka.
 
• **Role of Gram Panchayats:** The state government has integrated **Panchayati Raj Institutions** to monitor and report child marriage cases, making the **village-level officers** accountable for prevention.
 
• **Legal Age:** Despite various debates, the legal age for marriage remains **18 for girls** and **21 for boys**. Any violation of this age criteria, even for an engagement, attracts the provisions of the **2025 Bill**.
 
• **Child Rights Protection:** The **Karnataka State Commission for Protection of Child Rights (KSCPCR)** played a pivotal role in recommending these amendments to address the **safety, health, and education** of the girl child.
</ul

questions.question: What is the rank of India in the Global Firepower Index 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fourth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India** has secured the **fourth** position in the **Global Firepower (GFP) Index 2025**, maintaining its status as one of the most powerful militaries in the world.
 
• The **Global Firepower Index** evaluates the military strength of **145 nations** based on over **60 individual factors** to determine a country's **PowerIndex (PwrIndx)** score.
 
• The ranking is based on a nation's potential war-making capability across **land, sea, and air** fought by **conventional means**; notably, nuclear capabilities are not factored into the score, though recognized.
 
• In the **2025** rankings, **India** follows the **United States** (1st), **Russia** (2nd), and **China** (3rd), rounding out the top four global military powers.
 
• A perfect **PwrIndx** score is **0.0000**, which is realistically unattainable; the closer a country is to this number, the more powerful its conventional military capability is considered.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Top 5 Global Powers:**
 
 
• The **United States** maintains the top spot due to its vast **technological advancements**, massive **defense budget**, and global logistics reach.
 
• **Russia** retains the second spot, largely due to its significant **land power** and armored vehicle units.
 
• **China** ranks third, showcasing rapid modernization in its **naval fleet** and **air force** capabilities.
 
• **South Korea** has seen a significant rise in recent years, holding the **fifth** position in **2025**, surpassing several European nations.
 
 
 
• **Measurement Parameters:**
 
 
• The index considers **Manpower** (available population for military service), **Airpower** (fighters, interceptors, and transport aircraft), and **Land Power** (tanks and artillery).
 
• **Naval Power** (submarines, aircraft carriers, and destroyers) and **Logistics** (labor force and port accessibility) are also critical components of the final score.
 
• **Financial factors** like **defense budget**, external debt, and purchasing power parity are analyzed to assess the sustainability of a prolonged conflict.
 
• **Geographical features** such as shared borders and coastline length are factored in as they impact defensive and offensive strategies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India's Military Assets:** India boasts one of the world's largest **active military personnel** counts and possesses significant **tank strength** and a versatile **Air Force**.
 
• **Regional Comparison:** In the **South Asian** context, India remains the most dominant force, followed by **Pakistan**, which has consistently appeared in the **Top 10** of the **Global Firepower Index** in recent years.
 
• **Exclusions:** The **GFP Index** does not take into account **nuclear stockpiles**, political leadership, or current diplomatic relations, focusing purely on **statistical military data**.
 
• **Report Year:** The **2025** report reflects the **modernization efforts** and procurement shifts of nations following recent global geopolitical tensions.
</ul

questions.question: Which tennis veteran became the first Asian male with 450 career wins by April 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kei Nishikori**__.

__
 
• **Kei Nishikori**, the veteran tennis star from **Japan**, etched his name in history by becoming the **first Asian male** player to reach the milestone of **450 career wins** on the **ATP Tour** by **April 2025**.
 
• This achievement highlights his longevity and dominance in professional tennis, particularly as he remains the most successful male singles player representing an Asian nation in the Open Era.
 
• The milestone was reached following a determined comeback from a series of debilitating **injuries**, including **hip surgery** in **2022** and subsequent **knee** and **ankle** issues that kept him out of consistent competition for much of **2023** and **2024**.
 
• Nishikori's **450th victory** serves as a testament to his resilience, further extending his record lead over other notable Asian players like **Vijay Amritraj** and **Paradorn Srichaphan**.
 
• Known for his exceptional **return of serve** and **backhand down the line**, Nishikori has maintained a high winning percentage throughout his career, which began professionally in **2007**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kei Nishikori (Japan):**
 
 
• Born on **December 29, 1989**, in **Shimane, Japan**, he moved to the **United States** at age 14 to train at the **IMG Academy**.
 
• He reached a career-high ranking of **World No. 4** in **March 2015** and became the first Asian-born man to reach a **Grand Slam singles final** at the **2014 US Open**.
 
• He has won **12 ATP singles titles** and earned an **Olympic Bronze Medal** for Japan at the **2016 Rio Olympics**.
 
 
 
• **Yuki Bhambri (India):**
 
 
• A former **Junior World No. 1** and winner of the **2009 Australian Open Junior** championship.
 
• While a top-tier talent for India, his singles career faced interruptions due to **tendonitis**. In recent years, he has successfully transitioned to the **ATP Doubles** circuit, achieving a top 50 ranking. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect regarding the 450 singles wins.***
 
 
 
• **Prajnesh Gunneswaran (India):**
 
 
• He reached a career-high ranking of **75** in **2019** and has been a key player for India in the **Davis Cup**.
 
• His career wins at the ATP main draw level are far below the 450 mark compared to Nishikori. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Somdev Devvarman (India):**
 
 
• A **three-time NCAA finalist** and **two-time champion**, he is one of India's most decorated collegiate and professional players.
 
• He won **Gold Medals** at both the **Commonwealth Games** and **Asian Games** in **2010** before retiring in **2017**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Winning Percentage:** Nishikori is famously ranked among the all-time leaders in **winning percentage in fifth sets**, showcasing his mental toughness in long matches.
 
• **Project 45:** Early in his career, he was nicknamed "Project 45" as he aimed to beat the record of **Shuzo Matsuoka**, who was the highest-ranked Japanese male player at **World No. 46**. Nishikori surpassed this in **2011**.
 
• **ATP Milestone Context:** Reaching **450 wins** puts a player in an elite bracket of the **ATP Tour**, usually occupied by Grand Slam champions and consistent Top 10 mainstays over a decade-long span.
</ul

questions.question: According to the UN Sustainable Development Report (SDR) 2025, what is India’s SDG Index Rank and Score?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rank 99 with score 66.95**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Sustainable Development Report (SDR) 2025**, **India** has achieved a global **Rank of 99**.
 
• The country has attained an overall **SDG Index Score of 66.95**, which indicates its cumulative progress toward achieving the **17 Sustainable Development Goals**.
 
• The **Sustainable Development Report** is an annual global assessment that tracks the performance of all **193 UN Member States** on the **SDGs**.
 
• The report is produced by the **Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)**, which has been operating since **2012** under the auspices of the **UN Secretary-General** and is led by **Professor Jeffrey Sachs**.
 
• The **SDG Index score** can be interpreted as the percentage of **SDG achievement**; a score of **66.95** suggests India is roughly **67%** of the way to the optimal target (100).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**
 
 
• The **SDGs**, also known as the **Global Goals**, were adopted by the **United Nations** in **2015** as a universal call to action to end poverty and protect the planet by **2030**.
 
• There are **17 specific goals**, including **SDG 1 (No Poverty)**, **SDG 5 (Gender Equality)**, and **SDG 13 (Climate Action)**.
 
 
 
• **The Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN):**
 
 
• This **organisation** mobilizes scientific and technical expertise from academia, civil society, and the private sector to support practical problem-solving for **sustainable development**.
 
• The **SDR** is the first worldwide study to assess where each country stands with regard to achieving the **Sustainable Development Goals**.
 
 
 
• **India's Domestic Monitoring:**
 
 
• In **India**, the **NITI Aayog** is the nodal agency responsible for overseeing the implementation of **SDGs**.
 
• It releases the **SDG India Index** annually to track the progress of **States** and **Union Territories**, ensuring competitive federalism in achieving **global targets**.
 
 
 
• **Global Leaders:**
 
 
• Historically, **Nordic countries** such as **Finland**, **Sweden**, and **Denmark** consistently rank at the top of the **SDG Index** due to robust social safety nets and environmental policies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Decade of Action:** The **United Nations** has termed the period from **2020 to 2030** as the **Decade of Action**, urging all countries to accelerate sustainable solutions to all the world’s biggest challenges.
 
• **Performance Indicators:** The **SDG Index** uses a wide range of data points, including **health outcomes**, **economic growth**, **educational attainment**, and **carbon emissions**, to provide a holistic view of national development.
 
• **SDR 2025 Context:** The **2025 report** emphasizes the need for **International Financial Architecture** reform to provide **developing nations** with the necessary **liquidity** and **investment** to reach the **2030 goals**.

• **Pandit Dindayal Upadhyay Indoor Stadium**:
 
 
• Located in the **Ghod Dod Road** area of **Surat**, it is a state-of-the-art indoor arena inaugurated in **1998**.
 
• It was the first of its kind in **Western India** to be fully air-conditioned and has a seating capacity of approximately **7,000** spectators.
 
• The stadium frequently hosts diverse events ranging from **badminton**, **volleyball**, and **table tennis** to cultural programs and international conventions.
 
 
 
• **Table Tennis Federation of India (TTFI)**:
 
 
• Established in **1926**, it is the governing body for table tennis in India and is a founder member of the **International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF)**.
 
• Headquartered in **New Delhi**, it oversees the development of the sport through various age-category nationals and the **Ultimate Table Tennis (UTT)** league.
 
 
 
• **Key Players in Indian Table Tennis**:
 
 
• **Achanta Sharath Kamal**: A legendary figure who holds the record for the most **Senior National titles (10)** and was awarded the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna** in **2022**.
 
• **Manika Batra**: The first Indian woman to win a common-wealth individual gold in table tennis and a recipient of the **Arjuna Award** and **Khel Ratna**.
 
 
 
• **Tournament Structure**:
 
 
• The Senior Nationals typically include **Men's Singles**, **Women's Singles**, **Men's Doubles**, **Women's Doubles**, and **Mixed Doubles** events.
 
• It also includes **Inter-State Team Championships** where various states and institutional teams like **Petroleum Sports Promotion Board (PSPB)** and **Railways (RSPB)** compete for top honors.
